requirements.title: cmd_verify_jsonl emits a terminal on every exit path
requirements.description:
Each arm of cmd_verify_jsonl (pass, fail, skipped, runtime error,
strict-signature-missing) emits exactly one hand-built terminal
(VERIFY_OK, VERIFY_FAIL, or VERIFY_ERROR) as its last stdout line
before returning the matching exit code.

requirements.title: emit_jsonl flushes stdout per event
requirements.description:
The emit_jsonl helper locks stdout, writes one compact JSON line +
'\n', and calls handle.flush() before returning. This is the only
path that writes JSONL to stdout; tracing is routed to stderr by
init_tracing.

requirements.title: cmd_verify_jsonl strict-mode ed25519 signature guard
requirements.description:
When strict is true and neither BUNDLE.sig nor --verify-key is
present, cmd_verify_jsonl emits VERIFY_STRICT_SIGNATURE_MISSING as a
finding followed by VERIFY_FAIL terminal, returning
EXIT_VERIFICATION_FAILURE (2). When --verify-key is supplied but the
key file is unreadable (I/O fault) or has invalid content (bad hex,
wrong length, invalid ed25519 point) the run terminates with
VERIFY_ERROR (exit 1) carrying the structured cause:
VERIFY_RUNTIME_READ_VERIFY_KEY for I/O, SIGN_INVALID_KEY /
SIGN_INVALID_SIGNATURE_HEX for parse. Successful key load with a
present BUNDLE.sig that fails ed25519 verification surfaces
VERIFY_SIGNATURE_INVALID + VERIFY_FAIL.

requirements.title: terminal_{ok,fail,error} construct fixed-code diagnostics
requirements.description:
The three terminal-builder helpers in cli/verify.rs hand-construct
Diagnostic { code = VERIFY_OK / VERIFY_FAIL / VERIFY_ERROR, severity,
message, location: None, fix_hint: None, subcommand: None }. The
code strings correspond 1:1 to the exit-code mapping in Schema
Rule 1.

requirements.title: OutputFormat::resolve folds --json + --format precedence
requirements.description:
resolve returns format_flag unchanged if it is not Human; otherwise
it returns Json when json_flag is true, else Human. Explicit
--format always wins over the legacy --json bool.

requirements.title: cmd_schema_show writes embedded schema source to stdout
requirements.description:
cmd_schema_show maps the CLI SchemaName to evidence_core::schema::Schema
and prints the include_str!()'d source verbatim. Schema::for_filename
deliberately returns None for diagnostic.schema.json so schema
validate never matches it by filename.

requirements.title: dispatch guard emits CLI_SUBCOMMAND_ERROR terminal
requirements.description:
When --format=jsonl is passed to any non-verify subcommand,
dispatch calls emit_unsupported_jsonl_terminal, which streams
CLI_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT (finding) then CLI_SUBCOMMAND_ERROR
(terminal, with subcommand field set), returning EXIT_ERROR. Stderr
stays silent.

requirements.title: default_trace_roots picks cert/trace or cert/trace
requirements.description:
default_trace_roots returns Option<Vec<String>> by probing for
./cert/trace/ then ./cert/trace/. cmd_trace calls it only when
--trace-roots is absent; explicit flag always wins. Logs chosen root
via tracing::info!.

requirements.title: cmd_check dispatches on --mode and argument shape
requirements.description:
cmd_check reads --mode (Auto/Source/Bundle, default Auto) and the
optional path arg (default "."). Auto precedence: SHA256SUMS at
PATH → bundle mode; else Cargo.toml at PATH → source mode; else
CLI_INVALID_ARGUMENT + VERIFY_FAIL terminal. Explicit mode always
wins; mismatch between mode and shape also errors cleanly.

requirements.title: RULES const + rules subcommand + rules_json()
requirements.description:
`evidence_core::rules` defines `RuleEntry { code, severity, domain,
has_fix_hint, terminal }`, the `Domain` enum (closed over code
prefixes), and `pub const RULES: &[RuleEntry]` exhaustively listing
every emittable code. `rules_json()` returns a deterministic
serialized form sorted by code. `cargo_evidence::cli::rules::cmd_rules`
renders either the JSON array (`--json`) or a human-readable table.
`--format=jsonl` is not supported (single JSON blob, not a stream)
and falls through to the existing `CLI_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT` guard.

requirements.title: cmd_floors runs the gate + JSONL support
requirements.description:
`cargo evidence floors [--format={human,jsonl}] [--json] [--base <ref>]`
reads cert/floors.toml, computes current measurements via
`evidence_core::floors`, compares each entry against its floor / ceiling,
and prints a per-dimension table in human mode, a deterministic
JSON array in `--json` mode, or one JSONL diagnostic per dimension in
`--format=jsonl` mode. Human + JSONL paths terminate with `FLOORS_OK`
or `FLOORS_FAIL`; any below-floor / above-ceiling emits
`FLOORS_BELOW_MIN` naming the dimension, current value, and committed
threshold; exit 2 if any failure. Non-failure dimensions emit
`FLOORS_DIMENSION_OK` in the JSONL stream. A `--base` flag scopes the
`[delta_ceilings]` check to the PR diff.

requirements.title: cmd_trace stream-emits one Diagnostic per LinkError
requirements.description:
When `trace --validate --format=jsonl` hits
`Err(TraceValidationError::Link { errors })`, the CLI handler
iterates `errors` and calls `emit_jsonl` once per variant with
`code = link_error.code()`, `severity = Error`, `message =
link_error.to_string()`, and a variant-specific `Location`.
Legacy `--json` mode keeps the prior aggregate shape (single
result object with a concatenated `message`) so shell consumers
that piped through `jq .message` aren't broken. Test-selector
resolution failures surface as `TRACE_SELECTOR_UNRESOLVED`
alongside Link-phase variants.

requirements.title: cmd_doctor subcommand implementation
requirements.description:
`cmd_doctor(args) -> Result<()>` in
`crates/cargo-evidence/src/cli/doctor.rs` runs each rigor check
in a fixed deterministic order, emitting one `Diagnostic` per
check via `evidence_core::diagnostic::emit_jsonl` with a `DOCTOR_*`
code. Severity is derived per check: trace / floors / boundary
failures are `error`; CI / merge-style / override-doc gaps are
`warning`. A check that passes emits an `info`-severity
`DOCTOR_*_OK` diagnostic so the stream shape stays "one line
per check" and downstream tooling can detect truncation.

Stream terminates with exactly one terminal diagnostic:
- `DOCTOR_OK` + exit 0 when no `error`-severity diagnostic fired
- `DOCTOR_FAIL` + exit 2 when at least one `error` fired
Per Schema Rule 1 + the existing `TERMINAL_CODES` contract.

`generate` wires doctor via a `precheck_doctor(&config)` call in
the `Profile::Cert | Profile::Record` branch; the call returns
`Err(BuilderError::DoctorFailed { codes: Vec<&'static str> })`
when the audit fails, and the main dispatch translates the error
into a `GENERATE_ERROR` terminal whose diagnostic enumerates the
per-check codes so the auditor gets full detail without re-
running doctor.

requirements.title: Pre-release detection at build time + verify-side refusal
requirements.description:
Four coupled sites:

- `crates/evidence-core/src/env/capture.rs` adds a module-scope
  `TOOL_IS_PRERELEASE: bool` computed from
  `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` by byte-scanning for `-` in
  const context. `env_fingerprint` appends `tool_prerelease:
  TOOL_IS_PRERELEASE` to the returned `EnvFingerprint`.
- `crates/evidence-core/src/env/fingerprint.rs` grows
  `tool_prerelease: bool` with `#[serde(default)]` so
  pre-PR-#60 bundles deserialize as `false`.
- `crates/evidence-core/src/verify/errors.rs` adds
  `VerifyError::PrereleaseToolDetected { profile,
  engine_crate_version }` with `DiagnosticCode` returning
  `"VERIFY_PRERELEASE_TOOL"`.
- `crates/evidence-core/src/verify/bundle.rs` reads
  `env.tool_prerelease` after `check_env_vs_index` and pushes
  the error on every profile — library stays policy-free.
- `crates/cargo-evidence/src/cli/verify.rs::cmd_verify_jsonl`
  partitions the error bag: `VERIFY_PRERELEASE_TOOL` on
  `Profile::Dev` → Warning stream + `VERIFY_OK` terminal +
  exit 0; same code on Cert/Record → Error + `VERIFY_FAIL` +
  exit 2. Every other VerifyError stays error-severity.
- `crates/cargo-evidence/src/cli/generate/phases.rs::init_builder`
  emits a warning-severity `VERIFY_PRERELEASE_TOOL` in
  cert/record profile when `TOOL_IS_PRERELEASE` is true. Same
  init_builder path emits `ENV_ENGINE_RELEASE_PROVENANCE`
  (Warning) on cert/record when `TOOL_BUILD_SOURCE_IS_RELEASE`
  is true — a `release-v<version>` engine_git_sha fallback
  carries weaker provenance than a git-source SHA and a
  cert-grade run should prefer `cargo install --git`.

requirements.title: resolve_llr_backlinks enriches TestOutcomeRecord + check_llr_test_selectors asserts reverse
requirements.description:
`evidence_core::trace::test_backlinks::resolve_llr_backlinks`
mutates a slice of `TestOutcomeRecord` in place, filling each
record's `requirement_uids` with the deduplicated union of
`TestEntry.traces_to` across every TestEntry whose
`all_selectors()` matches `{module_path}::{name}` (exact or
`::`-boundary prefix, sibling-module-no-match pinned by test).

`cargo_evidence::cli::generate::test_outcomes::enrich_and_write_test_outcomes`
accumulates `TestEntry` across every configured trace root,
calls `EvidenceBuilder::enrich_test_outcomes_with_llrs`, then
writes `tests/test_outcomes.jsonl` with the populated records.
Runs in Phase 6b after trace validation.

`evidence_core::verify::llr_selectors::check_llr_test_selectors`
reads `bundle/trace/llr.toml` + `tests/test_outcomes.jsonl`
inside `verify_bundle_with_key`, accumulates the set of
`requirement_uids` across all records, then for every LLR with
`verification_methods.contains("test")` AND a non-None `uid`,
asserts the uid is present in the set. Missing → push
`VerifyError::LlrTestSelectorUnresolved { llr_uid, llr_id }`.
Skip silently when the JSONL file is absent (older bundles).
Empty-string uids are treated the same as `None` for
defense-in-depth against corrupt trace data.

`cargo_evidence::cli::verify::skipped_notices::maybe_emit_llr_check_skipped_no_outcomes`
emits `VERIFY_LLR_CHECK_SKIPPED_NO_OUTCOMES` (Info) on the
`VerifyResult::Pass` path when `tests/test_outcomes.jsonl` is
absent — the library-side check silently returned; this notice
surfaces that skip so an auditor can distinguish "check ran and
passed" from "check didn't run."

requirements.title: coverage subprocess + llvm-cov JSON parser + bundle write
requirements.description:
`evidence_core::coverage::report::CoverageReport` models the
typed wire shape of `coverage/coverage_summary.json`. Top-level
fields: `schema_version: String` (pinned to
`schema_versions::COVERAGE`), `measurements: Vec<Measurement>`.
Each `Measurement` carries a `level: CoverageLevel` enum with
four variants (`statement`, `branch`, `pattern_decision`,
`mcdc` — the latter two reserved, not emitted), plus
`engine: String`, `engine_version: String`, and
`per_file: Vec<FileMeasurement>`. Each `FileMeasurement` has a
workspace-relative `path: String`, `lines: LineCoverage
{covered, total}`, `branches: Option<BranchCoverage {covered,
total}>`, `decisions: Vec<DecisionCoverage>`, and
`conditions: Vec<ConditionCoverage>`. `branches` is `Some` at
`CoverageLevel::Branch` and `None` at `Statement` —
aggregation over a Branch measurement reads the `branches`
field, never `lines`. `decisions` / `conditions` stay reserved
for v2 pattern-decision / MC/DC; both are empty today
regardless of level.

`evidence_core::coverage::llvm_cov_json::parse_llvm_cov_export`
consumes `cargo-llvm-cov`'s JSON export format (documented
shape: `{data: [{files: [...], functions: [...], totals: {...}}],
version, cargo_llvm_cov: {version}}`), normalizes absolute file
paths to workspace-relative, and returns a `CoverageReport` with
one measurement per requested level. Filename normalization
strips the workspace root prefix deterministically so hashes are
cross-host stable.

`cargo_evidence::cli::generate::coverage_phase::run_coverage_phase`
is the new Phase 5b of `cmd_generate`. It is invoked after the
plain `cargo test` phase when `CoverageChoice != None`. The
function spawns `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --json --output-path
<tmp.json> --lcov --output-path <tmp.lcov>` (via
`std::process::Command`), parses the JSON, and stages both files
into the builder via `EvidenceBuilder::set_coverage_report` and
`EvidenceBuilder::stage_coverage_lcov`. On ENOENT (binary
missing) the phase emits a `COVERAGE_LLVMCOV_MISSING`
diagnostic whose severity is Warning for `Profile::Dev` and
Error for `Profile::Cert` / `Profile::Record`; on JSON parse
failure it emits `COVERAGE_PARSE_FAILED` (always Error).
Successful completion emits `COVERAGE_OK` (Info non-terminal)
naming the engine version and per-level line counts.

requirements.title: Wire derived entries at cli/trace.rs + cli/generate/phases.rs
requirements.description:
At `cli/trace.rs:120` and `cli/generate/phases.rs:313`, replace
the `&[]` placeholder in the `validate_trace_links_with_policy`
call with `derived.as_ref().map(|d| d.requirements.as_slice()).unwrap_or(&[])`
(pulling `derived` from the `TraceFiles` destructure in
both places). The doctor's `check_trace` at
`cli/doctor/checks.rs:43-45` already does the correct thing
(accumulates `files.derived.map(|d| d.requirements)` across
every root); this LLR brings the other two callsites to
parity. No new diagnostic codes — existing Link-phase errors
(`TRACE_DANGLING_LINK`, etc.) already fire correctly once the
derived slice is present.

requirements.title: aggregate_lines_percent sums per_file[].lines over a Statement-level Measurement
requirements.description:
`aggregate_lines_percent(m: &Measurement) -> f64` computes
`sum(per_file[].lines.covered) / sum(per_file[].lines.total)
* 100.0`. Used by the Statement-level arm of
`threshold_violations` (enforcement side) and by
`EvidenceBuilder::coverage_statement_percent` (compliance-
report side). The two callsites are textually similar but
non-shared because the enforcement arm lives in
`cargo-evidence` (needs the CLI-side policy context) and the
compliance arm lives in `evidence-core` (populates the wire
`CoverageSummary`). Both are asserted by the same test
triplet to prevent drift.

Zero denominator (no executable lines across all files)
returns `0.0`. Without this guard, `u64::sum() / u64::sum()`
would panic on division-by-zero in release mode and return
NaN in f64 — either one breaks the `< threshold` comparison
silently (NaN comparisons always return false, so a NaN
"current" would never trigger a violation, hiding the gap).

The function has no parameter for the measurement level
because the level is implicit in the caller's dispatch —
passing a Branch-level `Measurement` here would sum that
measurement's `lines` field, which is populated but
semantically secondary at Branch level. The dispatch in
`threshold_violations` is what binds "Statement level uses
lines" to the policy.

requirements.title: aggregate_branches_percent sums per_file[].branches over a Branch-level Measurement
requirements.description:
`aggregate_branches_percent(m: &Measurement) -> f64` computes
`sum(per_file[].branches.map_or(0, |b| b.covered)) /
sum(per_file[].branches.map_or(0, |b| b.total)) * 100.0`.
Files where `branches` is `None` contribute `0/0` (no
contribution) rather than `0/total` (which would pull the
aggregate toward zero). This distinction matters when a
Branch-level measurement is assembled from a mixed parser
run where some files legitimately lacked branch data.

**This function is the core of the bugfix.** Pre-fix, the
Branch-level arm of `threshold_violations` called a shared
`aggregate_percent` that always summed `lines.*`. A file at
95% lines / 50% branches looked like 95% branch coverage —
DAL-B's 85% branch minimum passed spuriously, and the tool
certified a bundle whose claim it could not mechanically
defend.

The symmetry with `aggregate_lines_percent` is deliberate but
not DRY: collapsing them into a generic `aggregate_percent(m,
|f| &f.lines)` would re-introduce the risk of a caller
passing the wrong field-accessor at call site. Two
single-purpose functions make the Branch vs Statement
distinction unmissable at every callsite.

Zero denominator → `0.0`, same rationale as LLR-057.

requirements.title: threshold_violations dispatches to level-appropriate aggregator; strict < comparison
requirements.description:
`threshold_violations(report: &CoverageReport, thresholds:
DalCoverageThresholds) -> Vec<ThresholdViolation>` iterates
over each `(level, Option<u8>)` threshold entry:

  1. Skip if `thresholds.<level>_percent` is `None` (DAL-D or
     dev). No violation recorded.
  2. Skip if no `Measurement` of that level exists in the
     report. No violation recorded — "measurement absent" is
     a config-layer issue, not a coverage-layer failure.
     Treating absence as 0% would mask the true problem
     (auditor gets COVERAGE_BELOW_THRESHOLD when they
     should have gotten a "configure your coverage=branch
     flag" signal).
  3. Compute `current = aggregate_<level>_percent(m)`.
  4. If `current < f64::from(threshold)`, append a
     `ThresholdViolation { dimension, current_percent,
     threshold_percent }`.

Comparison is strict `<`, not `<=`. DO-178C A-7 minima are
stated inclusively ("statement coverage shall be ≥ 90% at
DAL-C"), so equality is compliant. This is a BVA case the
test triplet pins — `current == threshold` must not fire.

The two-level dispatch (statement uses
`aggregate_lines_percent`, branch uses
`aggregate_branches_percent`) is what enforces the level/
field binding at the policy layer. The dispatcher is the
only place in the threshold-enforcement chain where that
binding is decided; changing it to use a shared aggregator
would be the regression path.

requirements.title: load_max_dal: max over dal_map values, fall back to default_dal on empty in_scope, D on load failure
requirements.description:
`load_max_dal(workspace: &Path) -> (Dal, bool)`:

  1. Load `<workspace>/cert/boundary.toml` via
     `BoundaryConfig::load`. On any load error (missing file,
     parse failure), return `(Dal::D, false)`. The `false`
     sentinel feeds the caller's fallback-note string; the
     matching `check_boundary` diagnostic names the root cause
     so this code stays silent on the load-fail path.
  2. Compute `cfg.dal_map().values().copied().max()` — the
     highest DAL across every in-scope crate (each in_scope
     entry mapped to its per-crate override or `default_dal`
     when no override is set; see `BoundaryConfig::dal_map`).
  3. If `max()` returns `None` (empty `in_scope`), fall back to
     `cfg.dal.default_dal`. This preserves user intent in the
     pre-scoping state — a boundary.toml with `in_scope = []`
     and `default_dal = "A"` is legitimate (project hasn't
     scoped crates yet); silently downgrading to `Dal::D` would
     surprise the auditor.
  4. Return `(dal, true)`.

The `unwrap_or(cfg.dal.default_dal)` is **not** a second bug-
opportunity — `default_dal` is already visited by every
dal_map entry that lacks an override, so the fallback affects
only the truly-empty-in_scope edge case.

Design note: the `Dal::D` hard floor on load failure is
stricter than `cfg.dal.default_dal` fallback on empty in_scope.
This asymmetry is deliberate — a missing/corrupt boundary.toml
means configuration intent is unknown, so the safest floor is
D. An empty `in_scope` with a loaded config means intent is
known; honoring it is the right behavior.

requirements.title: validate_trace_links_phase returns TraceValidationResult; write_compliance_reports takes trace_validation_passed: bool
requirements.description:
`TraceValidationResult { passed: bool, short_circuit:
Option<i32> }` is the return type of
`validate_trace_links_phase`. Three-state encoding:

  - `Passed = { passed: true, short_circuit: None }` — every
    root validated; A3-6 claim "Met" is defensible.
  - `WarnedContinuing = { passed: false, short_circuit: None }`
    — non-strict profile saw a failure; caller threads
    `passed: false` to compliance; A3-6 claim becomes
    "Partial" per `determine_objective_status`.
  - `StrictFailed = { passed: false, short_circuit: Some(code)
    }` — strict profile short-circuited; caller returns
    `code` before running any later phase, so compliance JSON
    is not written for this run.

`write_compliance_reports` signature adds a required
`trace_validation_passed: bool` parameter forwarded into
`CrateEvidence.trace_validation_passed`. The signature change
is load-bearing: removing the parameter to re-introduce a
hardcoded literal would be a visible PR diff, not a silent
in-function change.

`read_all_trace_files` read-failure path (missing or
corrupt trace TOML) also flips `passed = false` under
non-strict profile — the pre-fix contract was
non-observable (returned `Ok(None)` either way); post-fix the
warned-continue semantics cover both validation failures and
read failures symmetrically.

requirements.title: verify --verify-key I/O failure emits VERIFY_RUNTIME_READ_VERIFY_KEY + VERIFY_ERROR terminal
requirements.description:
`cmd_verify_jsonl` and `cmd_verify` both load the
`--verify-key` file before calling `verify_bundle_with_key`.
When `fs::read(path)` fails (missing or unreadable key), the
verify pipeline has already started its user-visible run, so
Schema Rule 1 (HLR-001) requires exactly one terminal on the
`--format=jsonl` stream. The handler emits a structured
`VERIFY_RUNTIME_READ_VERIFY_KEY` finding (path + os-error
message), then the `VERIFY_ERROR` terminal, then exits 1.

The code is distinct from `VERIFY_RUNTIME_READ_FILE` because
the failure precedes any bundle-file access — the path
carried in the diagnostic is the user-supplied key path, not
a bundle-relative path. The bijection between
`VerifyRuntimeError` variants and `VERIFY_RUNTIME_*` codes
stays one-to-one.

For `--format=human` and `--format=json` the same shape
applies via `fail_verify(&bundle_path, "verify_key", ...,
EXIT_ERROR)` so all three formats agree (HLR-016): the
run records a `verify_key` check at status `fail` with the
os-error message, prints `error: reading verify key from
<path>` to stderr (human) or wraps the failure in
`VerifyOutput { success: false, error: Some(msg) }` (json),
and exits 1.

requirements.title: check_dal_a_mcdc_evidence + enforce_dal_qualification gate
requirements.description:
Library side: `evidence_core::check_dal_a_mcdc_evidence(dal_map,
auxiliary_mcdc_tool)` returns `Ok(())` when no in-scope crate is
at DAL-A OR an `AuxiliaryMcdcTool` reference is present.
Returns `BoundaryCheckError::DalAMissingAuxiliaryMcdc { dal_a_crates,
count }` (code `BOUNDARY_DAL_A_MISSING_AUXILIARY_MCDC`)
otherwise. Library is policy-free — the dev/cert severity split
lives at the CLI layer.

CLI side: `enforce_dal_qualification(derived, profile,
json_output)` is called from `cmd_generate` immediately after
`enforce_boundary_policy`. On `Profile::Dev` a violation emits
a one-line Warning to stderr and the run proceeds. On
`Profile::Cert` / `Profile::Record` the violation triggers the
standard failure envelope (`fail` helper) and returns
`Ok(Some(EXIT_ERROR))` so the orchestrator short-circuits
before bundle assembly.

The message names every offender crate, points at the three
remediation paths (record auxiliary tool, lower DAL, wait for
upstream rustc), and cites rust-lang/rust#144999 +
rust-lang/rust#124144 so the auditor can verify the upstream
state independently.

`AuxiliaryMcdcTool` is a public type in
`evidence_core::policy::dal` carrying `name`, optional
`qualification_id`, and optional `report` (bundle-relative
path). `boundary.toml` reads it under `[dal.auxiliary_mcdc_tool]`
via serde.

requirements.title: main.rs --help intercept reuses clap's render tree
requirements.description:
`crates/cargo-evidence/src/main.rs`'s `-h` / `--help` intercept builds
a `clap::Command` for the `EvidenceArgs` parser and renders its
long-help directly, instead of printing a hand-typed redirect stub.

Concretely: the intercept calls `EvidenceArgs::command()` (the
clap-generated `CommandFactory` impl), prepends a one-line banner
naming the binary version and the dual invocation form
(`cargo evidence` + direct), then writes the long-form help via
`cmd.write_long_help(&mut stdout)`. The result includes clap's auto-
generated `Commands:` block — every variant of the `Commands` enum
in `cli::args` appears with its `#[command(about = …)]` description.

Output stays under 80-column wrap-friendly when terminal width is
fixed (clap's default render); this is a UX courtesy, not a
testable contract — the test pins only that each subcommand name
appears at least once in the rendered output.

Exit code: `0` on success, matching clap's auto-help convention.

The intercept lives at the top of `main()` (before the
`CargoCli::parse()` call) because the cargo subcommand dispatch form
(`cargo-evidence evidence …`) and the direct form
(`cargo-evidence --help`) take different argv shapes — clap's
`CargoCli::parse()` accepts only the dispatch form. The intercept's
`std::env::args().nth(1)` peek catches the direct form before clap
errors out.

requirements.title: cmd_keygen create + rotate dispatch
requirements.description:
cmd_keygen branches on the `rotate` flag. The create branch refuses if
either signing.key or signing.pub already exists (Outcome::RefusedExists
→ KEYGEN_KEY_EXISTS finding + KEYGEN_FAIL terminal, exit 1). The rotate
branch refuses if either file is missing (Outcome::RefusedRotateMissing
→ same code pair) and refuses up-front if --reason is missing (top-level
anyhow error). On success, both branches generate a fresh keypair via
evidence_core::{generate_signing_key, write_signing_key,
write_verifying_key}, best-effort chmod 600 on signing.key (Unix only),
and emit KEYGEN_OK; the rotate branch additionally appends a single
line to KEY-ROTATION-LOG carrying timestamp + new pubkey hex + reason.
If the OS randomness source is unavailable while drawing the key seed,
generate_signing_key surfaces SIGN_KEYGEN_ENTROPY, which propagates to
the KEYGEN_FAIL terminal rather than aborting the process.

requirements.title: finalize::check_pubkey_anchor refuses on mismatch
requirements.description:
After writing BUNDLE.sig, the finalize phase calls check_pubkey_anchor
with the just-used signing key. When `cert/signing.pub` exists the
function reads it via evidence_core::read_verifying_key and compares
its 32-byte representation to signing_key.verifying_key().to_bytes().
Mismatch returns an anyhow error carrying SIGN_PUBKEY_ANCHOR_MISMATCH
and the two paths involved; missing anchor file is a no-op (Ok(())).
The inner check_pubkey_anchor_at takes the anchor path explicitly so
unit tests can drive comparisons against tempdir fixtures rather than
the real cert/signing.pub.

requirements.title: cli::context wires CLI verb to context_for + emits CONTEXT_* terminals
requirements.description:
`cmd_context(positional, --crate, --module, format)` parses the
selector inputs (positional wins; otherwise `--crate` then
`--module`), calls `evidence_core::context::resolve_selector`, then
`context_for`, and renders the result. Human mode prints a compact
table; `--json` emits the report as a single pretty-printed blob;
`--format=jsonl` emits one compact report-line on stdout, one
`Diagnostic` per `ContextWarning` (severity = warning), and a
hand-built `CONTEXT_OK` / `CONTEXT_FAIL` / `CONTEXT_ERROR` terminal
on the last line. Exit codes: 0 for `CONTEXT_OK` (also the
`CONTEXT_NO_TRACE_CONFIGURED` graceful path), 1 for `CONTEXT_ERROR`,
2 for `CONTEXT_FAIL`. The three terminals are registered in
`evidence_core::TERMINAL_CODES`.

requirements.title: context content codes register in RULES and gate the golden wire shape
requirements.description:
The five content-level `CONTEXT_*` codes are registered in
`evidence_core::RULES` under the `Context` domain. The CLI's
`cmd_context` emits each at the right point: `CONTEXT_AMBIGUOUS_SELECTOR`
(warning) when the resolver records skipped alternates;
`CONTEXT_NO_REQUIREMENTS_FOR_SELECTOR` (warning) when a non-workspace
selector matches zero LLRs; `CONTEXT_SELECTOR_OUT_OF_SCOPE` (error)
when the resolver rejects an unrecognized input;
`CONTEXT_NO_TRACE_CONFIGURED` (info) when `cert/trace/` is missing;
`CONTEXT_RUNTIME_ERROR` (error) for the runtime / I/O variants of
`ContextError` (unreadable `Cargo.toml`, `canonicalize` failure on a
parent dir, underlying trace TOML read error) — distinct from
`CONTEXT_SELECTOR_OUT_OF_SCOPE` so an agent can tell user-typo from
tool-fault. A golden fixture at
`crates/cargo-evidence/tests/fixtures/golden_context.json` is byte-
diffed by the integration test, regenerated via
`tools/regen-golden-fixtures.sh`. Drift in the wire shape fires the
fixture diff with a line-numbered error.

requirements.title: write_agent_context_files emits root CLAUDE.md + .claude/settings.json
requirements.description:
`cmd_init` accepts an `agent_context: bool` parameter derived from
the clap flag pair `--with-agent-context` / `--no-agent-context`
(mutually exclusive via `conflicts_with`; default on). When true,
the parent dispatches to `write_agent_context_files(root, jsonl)`
which:
  - writes a starter `CLAUDE.md` at the root (lean ≤30 lines,
    rendered by `render_root_claude_md`) — title naming the
    project + `evidence_context` / `cargo evidence context`
    pointer + per-crate-CLAUDE.md guidance, no project rules;
  - writes `.claude/settings.json` registering `evidence-mcp` as
    an MCP server and adding a `permissions.deny` entry for
    `evidence/**` (the default output dir).
Both writes are skipped when the target file already exists; the
existing file is never clobbered. When `.claude/settings.json`
already exists, a single info line on stderr explains the merge
the user would do by hand. Each successful write goes through
`emit_template_written` so JSONL consumers see one
`INIT_TEMPLATE_WRITTEN` per file in the same stream as the
`cert/` emissions, terminating with the standard `INIT_OK`.

requirements.title: package-name -> manifest-dir resolution + control-input planning + generate-time fail-closed
requirements.description:
`resolve_in_scope_units` parses `cargo metadata` and maps each
in-scope package name to its workspace-relative manifest
directory via `manifest_path`, failing closed with
`MissingPackage` (name absent) or `PathEscape` (manifest not
under `workspace_root`).

`assemble_input_plan` merges the per-unit `git ls-files` results,
the declared required inputs (`boundary.toml` `[inputs].required`),
and the `WORKSPACE_CONTROL_PATHSPECS` results into a deduplicated,
provenance-tagged, sorted set (precedence unit > declared-required
> control), failing closed with `EmptyScope` (a unit resolved to
zero files) or `NoInputs` (an empty total). Declared required
inputs are existence-checked against the workspace root
(`check_required_inputs_exist`) and fail closed with
`MissingRequiredInput` — a git-ignored generated input that is
required but absent cannot be silently dropped.

`build_input_plan_blocking` orchestrates the subprocess calls and
the pure helpers. `hash_in_scope_sources` consumes the plan,
hashing each entry into `inputs_hashes.json`; strict (cert/record)
mode propagates any planning error as a generate failure, so a
cert bundle can never record an empty or mis-resolved source
baseline.

requirements.title: nextest libtest-json-plus parser preserves per-test identity
requirements.description:
`parse_nextest_libtest_json` reads nextest's `libtest-json-plus`
stream: `test` events (`{crate}::{binary}${module::path::name}`)
become `TestOutcomeRecord`s with package, binary, harness, and a
`module_path` reconstructed to begin with the binary, so
`{module_path}::{name}` equals the trace `test_selector` format;
`suite` events supply the aggregate `TestSummary`. nextest may emit
more than one `suite` summary for the same binary when it partitions
that binary's tests; suite counts are reduced per binary identity
(`passed`/`failed` summed over disjoint partitions, `ignored` and
`filtered_out` reduced as whole-binary tallies) so a partitioned
binary does not double-count and `reconcile` stays exact against the
per-test records. Per-test `exec_time` is deliberately not recorded
and records are sorted, so `test_outcomes.jsonl` stays
byte-deterministic (SYS-003).

`run_tests_and_capture` runs `cargo nextest run --workspace
--no-fail-fast --message-format libtest-json-plus` through the
builder's `run_capture` and feeds its stdout to the parser.

requirements.title: generator closure runs the release verifier before emitting GENERATE_OK
requirements.description:
After `finalize_and_sign`, `generator_closure` runs `verify_bundle`
against the just-written bundle. If the verifier rejects it, generate
emits `GENERATE_FAIL` and returns a non-zero exit instead of
`GENERATE_OK` — a generated bundle is not complete when the same tool
rejects the unchanged bundle. `verify_error_blocks_generate` mirrors
`verify`'s severity partition: a `PrereleaseToolDetected` finding is
non-blocking on `dev` only; every other finding, and all findings on
cert/record, blocks.

requirements.title: compiler-artifact inventory hashes workspace deliverables into outputs_hashes.json
requirements.description:
`parse_workspace_artifacts` reads `cargo build
--message-format=json` output, keeping `compiler-artifact`
messages whose `package_id` is an exact `cargo metadata`
`workspace_members` entry and whose target is a `lib` or `bin`.
Every produced filename becomes an `OutputArtifact { key, path }`
keyed by its path relative to cargo's `target_directory` — never
an absolute path. It fails closed on a malformed build message
(`MalformedMessage`) or an artifact outside `target_directory`
(`ArtifactOutsideTargetDir`) rather than silently skipping;
results are sorted and deduplicated for determinism.

`inventory_outputs_blocking` reads `workspace_members` and
`target_directory` from `cargo metadata`, then builds with the
bundle's recipe — cert/record build `--release --locked` so the
inventory attests the deliverable and a pinned dependency graph,
not an implicit debug build. `inventory_and_hash_outputs` hashes
each artifact into `outputs_hashes.json` via `builder.add_output`;
strict mode fails closed on zero deliverables or an unhashable
artifact. The inventory does its own build, so it is independent of
the test phase: `should_inventory` runs it on a full generate,
under `--skip-tests --inventory-outputs`, or unconditionally in
strict (cert/record) mode.

requirements.title: matrix view projects canonical corpus nodes and edges into the shared renderer
requirements.description:
`generate_corpus_traceability_matrix` constructs the matrix view by
iterating `CorpusGraph`: requirement layers select HLR and LLR rows,
test nodes select test rows, and canonical `DerivesFrom` and
`Verifies` edges supply relationships. Graph nodes retain the
presentation metadata needed for exact report parity. Both the
legacy entry projection and corpus projection feed one renderer, so
headers, annotations, tables, coverage counts, gaps, and ordering
cannot drift between two rendering implementations.

Bundle generation adapts the parsed legacy trace into a graph,
validates it, and calls the corpus generator. The existing
`generate_traceability_matrix` function retains its signature for
downstream compatibility.
